problems.problem: SYSTEMIC DARK DRIFT, 46 of 109 sites. I read app/globals.css myself: --text-body is declared once at line 53 as light-dark(#4a443b, #cfc7bb), so its DARK value is #cfc7bb. That makes the 63 #cfc7bb decisions genuine byte-identical no-ops (verified line by line; the classifier's darkIdentical:true is correct on all 63). But the 37 #d8d8de and 9 #d3d3da decisions all carry darkIdentical:false and every one of them CHANGES dark. #d8d8de -> #cfc7bb drops contrast on --bg (#0a0a0b) from 13.94:1 to 12.16:1; #d3d3da -> #cfc7bb drops it from 13.13:1 to 12.16:1. Luminance is the smaller half of it: #d8d8de and #d3d3da are cool blue-greys (B > R = G) and #cfc7bb is a warm beige (R > G > B), so this is a visible hue rotation across 46 sites in dark mode, not a rounding. Per HARD RULE 1 this is the blessed three-grey consolidation and the classifier does flag it explicitly at every one of the 46 sites (I checked each note individually — none is silently merged), so it is admissible. I am recording it so the drift is signed off with its real magnitude rather than waved through on the 'darkIdentical' column. The eight most visible instances are data cells that sit beside cool var(--text-muted) #9b9ba3 siblings in the same table row, where the warm shift reads as a temperature mismatch rather than a tone change: records.module.css:204 (.tour) and :209 (.tickets), tours.module.css:206 (.dCity), :212 (.dCap), :273 (.tourCell), :278 (.tickets), revenue.module.css:133 (.tour), mobileHome.module.css:422 (.boardName). Coverage itself is complete and correct: grep finds exactly 63 + 37 + 9 = 109 in-scope occurrences, matching globals.css:51-52's own tally, and the 64th #cfc7bb (app/lib/statCardImage.tsx:280) is rightly excluded as a permanently-dark ImageResponse render.
problems.claimed: 46 sites: #d8d8de / #d3d3da -> var(--text-body), 'dark shifts to #cfc7bb by design'
problems.correction: Accept as the table's blessed consolidation, but record it as a real dark-mode change, not a no-op: 46 sites move from a cool grey to a warm beige, ~13% contrast loss (13.94:1 -> 12.16:1). If dark must be a strict pixel no-op for this migration, the 37 #d8d8de and 9 #d3d3da sites need their own tokens (--text-body-cool at light-dark(#4a443b, #d8d8de)) instead; otherwise sign off explicitly on the 46-site warming.

problems.problem: BREAKS DARK AT ALL 13 COLOR-MIX SITES. The new token --shadow-strength is a unitless NUMBER, and the proposal gives it a dark and a light value without saying how it is declared. globals.css:249-252 carries its own warning on exactly this point ("light-dark() takes COLOURS") and is why --shadow and --glow already live in the :root[data-theme="light"] override block. An implementer following the file's dominant convention writes `--shadow-strength: light-dark(1, 0.31)`, which is not a valid <color> and not a valid <number>. Custom properties parse anything, so the failure surfaces at substitution: `calc(55% * light-dark(1, 0.31))` is invalid, the color-mix is invalid, and the whole box-shadow declaration becomes invalid-at-computed-value-time -> `unset` -> box-shadow: none. Dark mode loses the shadow entirely at all 13 sites, silently, with no CSS error. This is a spec gap in the new token, not a hypothetical: nothing in the proposal rules the wrong form out.
problems.claimed: --shadow-strength, dark 1 / light 0.31
problems.correction: The token spec must state the declaration form explicitly: `:root { --shadow-strength: 1; }` alongside the other :root tokens, and `--shadow-strength: 0.31;` added INSIDE the existing `:root[data-theme="light"]` block at globals.css:253-256 (which already holds --shadow and --glow for the same reason). --shadow-base is a colour and may use the normal form, `--shadow-base: light-dark(#17140f, #000000);`. With that declaration, dark computes calc(A% * 1) = A% and color-mix(in srgb, #000000 A%, transparent) unpremultiplies to rgba(0,0,0,A) — byte-identical at all 13 sites (55/55/50/65/55/60/45/45/45/50/62/45/55, each verified against the file).

problems.problem: DARK DRIFT, 16 DECLARATIONS. --ink-on-gold is declared at globals.css:50 as a flat `#14100a` with NO light-dark() wrapper — it is #14100a in BOTH modes. Rule 1 permits a non-identical consolidation only for the three reading-text greys (#cfc7bb / #d8d8de / #d3d3da) — #000 -> #14100a is not on that list, and the table's own DARK column for --ink-on-gold is therefore not 'today's value' at these sites. Sixteen declarations: mobileAnalysis 232/233, mobileApi 218/219, mobileCerts 418/419, mobileDeepPage 317/318, mobileMethodology 215/216, mobileMusic 189/190, mobileOfficialCharts 376/377, mobileRevenue 256/257, mobileTourMap 177/178, mobileTours 272/273. problems.correction: Either (a) declare it as `--ink-on-gold: light-dark(#14100a, #000000);` so dark is a byte no-op and paper still gets the warm ink, or (b) leave all 16 literals as #000 — the light-mode defect at these buttons is the BACKGROUND (`background-color: var(--gold)` at mobileAnalysis:230, mobileApi:216, mobileCerts:416, mobileDeepPage:315, mobileMethodology:213, mobileMusic:187, mobileOfficialCharts:374, mobileRevenue:254, mobileTourMap:175, mobileTours:270, which the table retires to --gold-ink #8a5a00 and which must become --gold-fill), not the ink. problems.problem: The 'CHROME — STAYS per design 4.3' call rests on a false read of the file. Line 57 is `background: linear-gradient(180deg, #111113 0%, var(--bg) 34%)`. --bg is light-dark(#f7f4ee, #0a0a0b), so from 34% down the sheet becomes #f7f4ee paper in light mode — it is NOT a --scrim surface and it is NOT covered by the established chrome mechanism, which is the token re-pin at globals.css:512-522 (`:root[data-theme="light"] .navbar, .navbar *`) — a block that re-pins --text/--text-muted/--text-body/--border/--bg-soft/--line/--gold-ink/--gold-display and notably does NOT re-pin --bg. Nothing in mobileNavSheet.module.css or any other module carries a data-theme rule (grepped). So the sheet themes to paper today and the frozen rgba(0,0,0,.5) will read as a hard black band under a white panel — the inverse of the caveat the note actually raises. Dark is a no-op either way, so this is not a dark break, but the justification is wrong and the light outcome is worse than described.
problems.claimed: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5) — chrome, stays
problems.correction: This decision cannot be settled inside the shadow family: it depends on whether the bg family makes .sheet genuinely dark chrome. If it does (background moves to --scrim plus a .navbar-style token re-pin), freeze the shadow as written and say so. If it does not (the var(--bg) at line 57 stays), the sheet is a themed surface and the shadow must take the color-mix like every other floating panel here.

problems.problem: The note's reason for theming this shadow — 'It is a floating notice over page content, not masthead/tab-bar chrome, so it themes' — skips what the surface actually is. Line 54: `background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(20, 16, 8, 0.96), rgba(9, 9, 11, 0.96))`. Two hardcoded near-black literals, no token, no light-dark. Unless the bg family retints them, light mode gets a near-black pill sitting on #f7f4ee with a rgba(23,20,15,.14) shadow that will not read at all. Same surface/shadow coupling the note correctly flagged for a human at map.module.css:246, but here it is asserted away rather than flagged. Dark is a clean no-op (55% -> rgba(0,0,0,.55)), so the shadow replacement itself is sound.
problems.claimed: color-mix(in srgb, var(--shadow-base) calc(55% * var(--shadow-strength)), transparent)
problems.correction: Keep the replacement but mark it dependent on the bg-family call for lines 54 (the two rgba near-blacks) and 52 (`border: 1px solid var(--gold)`, which the table retires to --gold-ink). If the pill stays hardcoded dark, this shadow must be frozen with it, not themed.

problems.problem: Two arithmetic claims in the notes are wrong, and one structural claim is overstated. (a) 0.45 x 0.31 = 0.1395, not 0.14 — the notes at this line and at todaysNumber.module.css:128 both say the light result lands 'exactly' on --shadow's paper alpha of .14, and the --shadow-strength rationale repeats it ('0.31 is derived, not invented — the exact ratio'). It is a 0.4% rounding, harmless, but 'exactly' is false and the derivation should not be presented as exact. (b) More substantive: a colour-only swap cannot pick up --shadow's paper GEOMETRY. globals.css:249-252 states the whole point of the --shadow override — 'a 50px shadow that reads as depth on black reads as dirt on white' — yet 11 of the 13 sites keep their dark-mode blur radii on paper (28px here, 34px, 40px, 44px, 50px, 70px at song.module.css:86), only dimmed. The two sites the classifier correctly spots as byte-identical to --shadow (statCardButton:39 and music.module.css:333, both `0 20px 50px rgba(0,0,0,.45)`) get the geometry via `box-shadow: var(--shadow)`; the other eleven do not.

problems.correction: State the alpha as ~0.1395 and drop 'exactly'. Separately, flag for the design owner that eleven ad-hoc geometries survive onto paper unchanged; if that is unacceptable, --shadow-base/--shadow-strength is the wrong shape and these need per-site light geometry (a second whole-value token, or a --shadow-sm/--shadow-lg pair) rather than a colour swap.

problems.problem: The note reaches the wrong conclusion after correctly identifying the risk. If the card stays dark, a rgba(23,20,15,.14) shadow under a near-opaque black card on #f7f4ee paper removes the separation it exists to provide, and the card reads as a sticker cut out of the page. The shadow's correctness is bound to the surface decision, exactly as the note itself argues for the nav sheet. Dark is a clean no-op (55% -> rgba(0,0,0,.55)).

problems.problem: UNFLAGGED BROKEN PAIR. .lede sits inside .hero above .heroScrim (line 126, z-index -1), whose horizontal gradient is HALF-THEMED: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--bg) 38%, rgba(10,10,11,0.78) 62%, rgba(10,10,11,0.35) 100%). problems.problem: UNFLAGGED BROKEN PAIR, desktop twin of the mobileCerts hero. .heroScrim (line 403) is again half-themed: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--bg) 40%, rgba(10,10,11,0.82) 66%, rgba(10,10,11,0.62) 100%), sitting over .heroArt (opacity .38) and .heroArtBlur. page.tsx line 140-150 puts .lede inside .heroCopy under that scrim. .lede is max-width:60ch (~600px at 17.5px) in the 1.3fr column of a 1.3fr/1fr grid; at a 1024-1200px viewport the copy column is only ~485-580px wide, so the lede fills it and its tail crosses the scrim's 40% solid-paper boundary into the ramp. problems.problem: The mapping's own flag is correct and I confirm it: .codeAttr is inside .codeBox, whose background is the hardcoded literal #0f0f11 (line 157). problems.claimed: var(--text-body) (flagged, resolution left open)

problems.problem: The mapping's flag is correct and I confirm the surface: .cardEvents li is inside .card (line 240), background rgba(12,10,9,0.97) — that is --scrim's colour family, on a position:fixed pointer-following tooltip. But the flag's "either the card themes to a paper surface or this text must stay light" misses that the card is already broken by tokens outside this family: .cardName (line 269) is var(--text) and .cardRegion (line 277) is var(--gold), both of which go dark ink on a 0.97-opaque near-black card in light mode. problems.claimed: var(--text-body) (flagged, resolution left open)

Map .card's background to var(--scrim) so it stays deliberately dark in both themes, and then LEAVE .cardEvents li at its #cfc7bb literal (or give it an explicit on-scrim text token) rather than var(--text-body) — and raise .cardName/.cardRegion as the same decision, since a themed card would break them instead.

problems.problem: The note's premise is factually wrong about the surface. It says "Cell background is var(--bg), or a 7% green wash on .boardNew — a tint, not a fill". It is not a tint: .boardCell sets background: var(--bg) (line 386) and .boardNew sets background: rgba(62,209,127,0.07) (line 400), which REPLACES the background-color rather than layering over it — same specificity, later in the file, and MobileHome.tsx line 236 applies both classes to the same element. So a .boardNew cell is 7% green composited over whatever is behind it, which is .board's own background: var(--rule) (line 378). In light mode that bed is rgba(23,20,15,0.48) over --bg, i.e. roughly #8d8a86 — a mid grey. #4a443b on ~#8d8a86 is about 2.5:1, under AA for 12.5px text. (In dark the same construction yields a light-grey cell today, so this is a pre-existing surface bug that theming makes a legibility failure rather than a curiosity.)

Flag .boardNew's background to the background family: it needs to layer the green over the cell ground, e.g. background: linear-gradient(color-mix(in srgb, var(--green) 7%, transparent), color-mix(in srgb, var(--green) 7%, transparent)), var(--bg) — the same two-layer pattern api.module.css:177 already uses for .blockGold. With that in place the cell is paper-plus-tint and body ink reads; without it the cell is the --rule bed and the name is marginal.

problems.claimed: var(--text-body)
problems.correction: Do not swap this line until .heroCard is decided. .heroCard is a permanently-dark surface, so use the pattern globals.css already ships for the masthead (:509-520): add `:root[data-theme="light"] .heroCard, :root[data-theme="light"] .heroCard * { --text: #f5f4f0; --text-body: #cfc7bb; --text-muted: #9b9ba3; --gold-ink: #ffb627; }` and THEN var(--text-body) is correct here and dark stays untouched. Note the same scrim traps .title, .kicker and .tagline (var(--gold) -> #8a5a00) in the same hero, so the fix belongs at .heroCard, not at this line.
problems.lens:
role-fit — verified the CSS property and the *surface* at each of the 109 sites. Coverage first: the 109 decisions account for exactly 113 minus 4 repo occurrences of #cfc7bb/#d8d8de/#d3d3da in app/**/*.css; the 4 unmapped are the token declarations themselves (globals.css:51,52,53 and the :root[data-theme="light"] .navbar override at :509). No site was missed and none is invented.

Property/role: all 109 are `color` on text, so --text-body is the right ROLE token at every site; none is a background, border, or gradient stop, so no fill/ink collapse (Rule 2) occurs in this family. problems.problem: The note recommends deleting --white-wash-base and folding these three sites onto var(--text), on the arithmetic "at 1.5% the delta is under 1/255". One byte of drift, in dark, at the SMALLEST alpha in the set. Over --bg-soft #141416 the red channel splits too (23.53 -> 24 vs 23.38 -> 23), and the other two sites (.02, .04) drift further. The same false claim is repeated in the --white-wash-base token rationale ("the cheapest fix may be to normalise the file onto --text instead of shipping this token").
problems.claimed: delta under 1/255, so this is the strongest candidate in the family for folding onto --text and deleting the proposed token
problems.correction: Ship --white-wash-base as proposed (dark #ffffff) and strike the fold-onto---text recommendation from both the site note and the token's `why`. The replacement as written is correct and byte-identical; only the suggested follow-up breaks dark. It says "--bg-raised (#24242a opaque) does NOT compute to the same colour here (5.5% #f5f0e8 over #0a0a0b ~ #191817)". The proposed color-mix is still a dark no-op, so nothing regresses - but on paper the seam bed becomes --rule light rgba(23,20,15,.48) over #f7f4ee ~ rgb(139,137,133), and a hovered TOC card lands around #84837f: a dark grey slab on white, not a lift.

problems.problem: The note's WARNING is factually wrong against the current globals.css and raises a needsHumanDecision for a non-problem. It claims "color: var(--text-muted) and border: var(--line) both flip to dark ink on a bar that stays dark, making the trigger nearly invisible in light mode." They do not flip. globals.css declares its entire token block on the selector list `:root, .navbar { color-scheme: dark; ... }` (globals.css:6-18), whose own comment states the reason: "Custom properties resolve light-dark() where they are DECLARED, not where they are used, which is why the island needs its own declaration and not just a color-scheme." Every light-dark() token therefore resolves to its DARK value inside the masthead. SearchPalette renders at Nav.tsx:48, inside <nav className="navbar"> (Nav.tsx:33), so it is inside the island. Acting on this warning - hardcoding the trigger's colours to defeat a flip that does not happen - would be a regression, defeating the island's stated future-proofing.

Consequence: this replacement is a pure no-op — it changes no pixel in either theme. Split --veil-base: the photo-scrim role wants a light value of #f7f4ee (page ground), the panel role wants #ffffff (--bg-soft's light value), so the popover reads as lifted off the map. As specified, --veil-base is asked to serve five distinct roles across its 11 sites — full-cover overlay (StatCardMaker:109, mobileStatCards:236, statCardButton:107), photo chip (mobileDeepPage:384, cars:290), inset panel (car.module.css:97), hero scrim (song.module.css:76 ×3) and floating popover (this line). problems.problem: In light the popover ground becomes #f7f4ee at 97%, while the map beneath it fills .off with var(--bg-soft-2) = #efeae1 — a delta of 8/10/13 in RGB. The floating detail card stops reading as floating; only the 1px --gold border separates it from the countries it is drawn over.

problems.claimed: Five new fixed/near-black tokens (--veil-base, --scrim-cool, --scrim-deep, --scrim-base, --photo-well) minted so dark stays byte-identical, while eight --ink-on-gold sites accept a dark shift
problems.correction: Apply one standard. --veil-base dark #0c0a09 vs --bg dark #0a0a0b differs by (2,0,2)/255 and its light value #f7f4ee is byte-identical to --bg's; --scrim-cool is #0a0a0b, byte-identical to --bg's dark; --photo-well dark #0a0908 differs from --bg by (0,1,3)/255 and its light value #e6e0d4 is byte-identical to --bg-raised's. Meanwhile #0a0a0b → --ink-on-gold #14100a is a (10,6,1)/255 shift accepted with a shrug. Either hold rule 1 strictly everywhere (and mint an --ink-on-gold-deep for the eight chip labels) or relax it consistently and collapse --veil-base/--scrim-cool/--photo-well onto --bg / --scrim / --bg-raised. Five single-purpose near-blacks whose roles are already named in the table is over-tokenization; the roles here are page-ground-at-alpha, chrome backdrop, and image matte, all of which exist.
problems.problem: Internally inconsistent application of hard rule 1: strict byte-identity is enforced for backgrounds nobody can distinguish, and waived for text where the delta is 2.5× larger. The result is a token set where role, not colour, has stopped deciding the name.

problems.claimed: color-mix(in srgb, var(--scrim-base) 90%, transparent), fixed in both modes, role "data"
problems.correction: Keeping it fixed is the right call for dark-identity, but state the light-mode consequence numerically and put it to the designer: 0.9-alpha near-black on #efeae1 gives a near-3:1-plus hairline grid, while every other structural line on the site is --rule at rgba(23,20,15,0.48). Propose --scrim-base as light-dark(rgba-equivalent of --rule at the map's weight, #0c0a09) or accept the divergence explicitly. Line 217 must move with it.
problems.problem: The role is 'structural line separating two data regions' — which is exactly what --rule is defined as (globals.css:32, 3.30:1, clears WCAG 3:1). Pinning it to a fixed 0.9 near-black gives the tour map a border weight roughly twice every other structural rule on the paper theme. Role-correct, weight-inconsistent.

problems.claimed: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 55%, transparent) — "Its text is var(--muted)… so the chip ground must theme with them"
problems.correction: Measure before asserting. --muted aliases --text-muted (globals.css:200), light #5f584f. On paper-at-55% over the grayscale(0.35) press shot the composite ground is ≈ rgb(185,183,180), giving 3.47:1 at 11px bold uppercase — below AA, and below today's dark measurement of 4.31:1 (itself already marginal). Take the chip ground to ~90%+ paper or var(--bg-soft). Same at line 231 (.pendingBadge, --muted on a tile dimmed to opacity 0.55, which is worse).
problems.problem: Same unmeasured 'themes with it' reasoning as the .anchorTag sites: a 55% wash is not a surface, and the ink that lands on it in light mode is a mid grey, not the near-white the dark render relies on.

problems.claimed: --scrim-cool, "sites: 4"
problems.correction: Five decisions reference --scrim-cool: mobileAfrobeatsHub:24 (.94), mobileLiveCharts:21 (.95), mobileMusic:21 (.95), mobileRecords:21 (.95) and mobileNavSheet:25 (.72). Correct the count, and note that at three alphas across five sites the token is being used as a base, not a value — which is fine, but then --scrim (an rgba, alpha baked in at .94) is the odd one out and should be re-expressed as a base plus color-mix so all chrome backdrops share one construction.
problems.problem: The token spec's own prose enumerates five uses while the sites field says 4. Minor, but the count is what a reviewer checks the patch against.

problems.claimed: var(--scrim) replacement for a literal inside the file header comment, listed as one of the 93 decisions
problems.correction: Drop it from the decision list or mark it documentation-only. It has no CSS property and therefore no role, and counting it inflates the family total. Update the prose as part of the patch, not as a mapping entry.
problems.problem: A comment is not a decision under a lens whose whole premise is 'the role is decided by the CSS property'. There is no property here.

newTokens.name: --green-dot
newTokens.why: The NON-TEXT half of the live-green split, already blessed in section 4.6. Carries the 5 solid dot fills (artist:522, afrobeats:332, mobileAfrobeatsHub:304, mobileCerts:580, liveCharts:7) and the 8 pulse/halo box-shadows that emanate from those dots. Keeping the dots on the darker #177a45 text green would make them read as ink specks rather than indicators on paper.

newTokens.name: --green (existing, retarget)
newTokens.why: No new declaration needed beyond the light-dark() retarget: --green already exists at globals.css:124 and --live is already an alias of it (globals.css:184). It serves all TEXT uses plus every arbitrary-alpha border and wash via color-mix, per the brief's own rgba(62,209,127,0.4) example.

newTokens.name: --shadow-base
newTokens.why: The ink of every ad-hoc drop shadow. --shadow is a whole box-shadow value and so cannot be reused at the 11 sites with their own geometry, and this patch swaps colour literals, not declarations. Paired with --shadow-strength in a color-mix it themes the hue while dark stays byte-identical (#000 at the original alpha). Light value is the same 23,20,15 ink --shadow's paper value already uses.

newTokens.name: --shadow-strength
newTokens.why: Alpha multiplier so one color-mix expression serves both modes: color-mix(in srgb, var(--shadow-base) calc(A% * var(--shadow-strength)), transparent). Dark leaves A untouched, so every replacement is a no-op. 0.31 is derived, not invented — it is the exact ratio --shadow already applies (.45 -> .14), so a .45 site reproduces --shadow's paper alpha of .14 and heavier sites scale in proportion. Avoids inventing a token per alpha (.45/.5/.55/.6/.62/.65 all appear).

newTokens.name: --ink-wash-base
newTokens.why: 22 of the 42 sites use rgba(245,240,232,a) — #f5f0e8, a warmer off-white than --text (#f5f4f0). Folding them onto var(--text) is a rounding: at the alphas in use (.045–.26) it moves G/B by up to 2/255 in dark mode, so it violates the byte-identical rule. This token carries the exact dark value and inverts to the same #17140f ink as --text on paper. It exists only to hold the drift; see needsHumanDecision — the team may prefer to retire #f5f0e8 into --text the way the three reading greys were retired into --text-body, which would delete this token.

newTokens.name: --white-wash-base
newTokens.why: liveCharts is the only file that washes with pure white (rgba(255,255,255,.015/.02/.04)) rather than the site's #f5f4f0/#f5f0e8. var(--text) is not byte-identical to #ffffff, so the same argument applies. Three sites only — the cheapest fix may be to normalise the file onto --text instead of shipping this token.

newTokens.name: --veil-base
newTokens.why: The themed counterpart to --scrim. Half the warm near-black rgba(12,10,9,α) sites are NOT chrome — song and car hero scrims, in-card failure overlays, photo badges, the map popover — and every one of them contains text that flips to ink, so their ground must flip to paper. --bg cannot serve them: --bg's dark value is #0a0a0b, so color-mix(var(--bg) 82%) would change the dark render. Dark #0c0a09 is byte-identical to today's base; light is the paper ground, so color-mix(in srgb, var(--veil-base) N%, transparent) darkens a photo in dark mode and lightens it on paper with one expression. (--bg already plays this role, byte-identically, for the 24 cool rgba(10,10,11,α) photo-scrim sites — no token needed there.)

newTokens.name: --scrim-cool
newTokens.why: Four chrome bars use the COOL near-black instead of --scrim's warm one, at two alphas: mobileAfrobeatsHub .backBar at .94, and mobileMusic / mobileRecords / mobileLiveCharts .backBar at .95, plus the nav-sheet dimmer at .72. Rule 4 says they stay dark, so they cannot be color-mix(var(--bg) …) — that would turn four mastheads and the sheet dimmer to paper. Fixed in both modes, it keeps dark byte-identical. Its dark value equals --bg's dark value, which is exactly why the naive fix is wrong and the token is worth having.

newTokens.name: --scrim-deep
newTokens.why: A fourth near-black base, rgba(8,7,6,α), used only by the two modal dimmers (statCardButton .backdrop at .5, music .backdrop at .6). A modal dimmer stays dark on paper, so it needs a fixed token; no existing one is byte-identical (#080706 vs --scrim's #0c0a09).

newTokens.name: --photo-well
newTokens.why: The opaque matte behind a car photograph (cars.module.css .tileImg and its mobile twin), visible only before the image paints. A fifth near-black that matches nothing in the table. Light value proposed as the --bg-raised paper so a loading tile does not flash a black rectangle in light mode — that light value is the open question, dark is byte-identical either way.

newTokens.name: --scrim-base
newTokens.why: The un-alpha'd warm scrim ink, FIXED in both modes, for the two map country-border strokes. They are dark-on-light hairlines even in dark mode (near-black on --bg-soft-2), so they must stay dark on paper too — the themed --veil-base would erase them. Also available as the fixed base for any future chrome scrim at an alpha other than .94.

newTokens.name: --gold-wash-base
newTokens.why: The table names it but globals.css does not declare it yet. It is the color-mix base for every translucent gold background, gradient stop and SVG data fill in this family (alphas 0.04-0.75). Dark #ffb627 makes every color-mix a byte-for-byte no-op; light #b07000 keeps a low-alpha tint perceptible on #f7f4ee, which #ffb627 at 5-30% is not.

newTokens.name: --gold-wash
newTokens.why: Seven sites sit at exactly 10% (FollowPanel:6, Sparkline:12, TimeSeriesChart:27, mobileHome:280/284, liveCharts:226, charts:292). The named token is byte-identical in dark and reads more clearly than a color-mix at those sites.

newTokens.name: --gold-glow-base
newTokens.why: The table retires --glow to none on paper, but 14 sites use gold box-shadows at four different geometries and alphas (0 0 26px .25 x11, 0 0 26px .24, 0 6px 18px .24, 0 0 44px .13) — none matches --glow's own value, and light-dark() cannot wrap a whole box-shadow because it only takes colors. One transparent-in-light base lets every glow keep its exact dark value via color-mix and disappear on paper, without inventing a token per alpha.

newTokens.name: --brand-accent
newTokens.why: Ayra Starr's raw brand colour, scoped to [data-brand="starrgirl"] per design 6.5. Declared for completeness as the non-text brand mark; every text site in this family takes --brand-accent-ink instead, which is why its site count is 0.

newTokens.name: --brand-accent-ink
newTokens.why: The light-safe form of Ayra's magenta for any text use. Light #a3157f measures 6.44:1 on #f7f4ee (5.90:1 on --bg-soft-2, 7.07:1 on #ffffff); dark #f06ae0 measures 7.39:1 on #0a0a0b. Covers artist.module.css 589 and 605 and mobileCerts.module.css 635, the last of which colours an 11px kicker and so sets the 4.5:1 floor.

newTokens.name: --brand-grad-1
newTokens.why: First stop of the Starrgirl name gradient. Because the gradient is clipped to text it must meet a text ratio: dark #ff5cd6 is 7.31:1 on #0a0a0b, light #a3157f is 6.44:1 on #f7f4ee.

newTokens.name: --brand-grad-2
newTokens.why: Middle stop (46%). Dark #c94ae8 is 5.30:1 on #0a0a0b; light #7d1a9e is 7.61:1 on #f7f4ee. Hue held so the magenta-to-violet sweep survives the flip.

newTokens.name: --brand-grad-3
newTokens.why: Violet stop (100%). Dark #9a5cf4 is 4.91:1 on #0a0a0b — the file's own comment explains it was already lifted off the artwork's #8b3df0 (3.79:1) for exactly this reason. Light #5b2bb5 is 7.78:1 on #f7f4ee.

newTokens.name: --brand-fill
newTokens.why: The active-filter pill's base fill on the Starrgirl mobile certifications screen. Does NOT flip: it carries an explicit white label at 6.70:1, which holds over paper as well as over black. Separate from --brand-accent because a fill and an ink are different roles even within one brand.

newTokens.name: --brand-fill-hi
newTokens.why: Top stop of the pill's deepened ramp. White on it is 5.11:1 — the worst point of the gradient, and what the file's comment is protecting. Frozen in both modes.

newTokens.name: --brand-fill-lo
newTokens.why: Bottom stop of the same ramp; white on it is 7.27:1. Frozen in both modes.

newTokens.name: --glow-base
newTokens.why: The warm halo base behind gold marks. color-mix(in srgb, var(--glow-base) 15%, transparent) computes rgba(232,176,75,0.15) byte-for-byte in dark and collapses to transparent in light, which is how section 4.6's 'glows do not exist on paper' is enforced without inventing a token per alpha. Serves about:97, mobileAbout:158 and page:31.

newTokens.name: --burnt
newTokens.why: The burnt-brown ink of the amber panels, distinct from --ink-on-gold (#14100a). Identical in both modes because four of its six sites sit on the closer panel, which is a gold fill that does not flip; the other two are decorative rings left over from when todaysNumber was on that same fill. Gives the six sites one home.

newTokens.name: --text-body-warm
newTokens.why: Warm reading grey used for 13-14px prose in api, mobileTours and cars. NOT one of the three greys the table retires, so consolidating into --text-body would shift dark by ~23 units of red. Light #544d43 is 7.59:1 on paper.

newTokens.name: --text-dim-warm
newTokens.why: One step quieter than --text-body-warm; used for dai-dai's group intro and (at 50%) for DaiDaiConquest's empty peak cells. Falls between --dim and --text-muted in dark but is warmer than either, so neither is byte-identical. Light #6f685f is 5.01:1 on paper.

newTokens.name: --peak-rest
newTokens.why: The fourth peak band ('beyond Top 40') as charts.module.css hardcodes it. Five units off --text-muted's #9b9ba3, so it cannot be folded in without breaking dark. Light matches --silver's light value so the cyan/silver/rest ramp stays ordered; 4.81:1 on paper.

newTokens.name: --sold-ink
newTokens.why: The v2 amber that marks a car as sold — 'a fact, not a warning'. Not --ember (#ff7a1a), so it needs its own token. Light #8f4700 is 6.23:1 on paper and 5.71:1 on --bg-soft-2, safe at the 10.5-11px the labels use.

newTokens.name: --error-ink
newTokens.why: The error-state red in appState, used at both 104px and icon size. Dark #e06a5c is not --red-ink's #e0796d, so rule 1 forbids the swap; light converges on #b3261e (5.95:1 on paper) so the two reds are indistinguishable on paper even though they differ in dark.

newTokens.name: --delta-down
newTokens.why: TrendDelta's falling figure and its arrow. Same reasoning as --error-ink: distinct in dark, converged in light.

newTokens.name: --move-down
newTokens.why: The live-charts falling-position marker — a fourth distinct dark red. Kept separate to preserve dark exactly; see needsHumanDecision about collapsing all four onto --red-ink.

newTokens.name: --live-dot
newTokens.why: The live-charts pulse. Its base must match .liveDot's own #35d07f, which is nine units of red away from --green-dot's #3ed17f, so a mix on --green-dot would not be a dark no-op. Light #1f9a5a matches --green-dot's light value, i.e. the two greens converge on paper.

newTokens.name: --bg-float
newTokens.why: The translucent floating puck surface (back-to-top). --bg-soft's dark #141416 is one unit of blue away, so I will not round it into an existing token.

newTokens.name: --code-bg
newTokens.why: The mobile API code well, which is inset below --bg-soft-2 in dark. Light takes --bg-soft-2's paper value, the correct inset tone. Watch the --gold-bright code text that sits in it.

newTokens.name: --card-glass
newTokens.why: The translucent spec/performance cards floating over the car stage. Proposed conditionally — see needsHumanDecision on whether the car detail pages theme at all.

needsHuman.question: This file uses #35d07f, a stray second live green that never got folded into the one-green consolidation described at app/globals.css:177-184. Tokenising lines 7 and 246 onto --green-dot / --green shifts dark by rgb(+9,+1,0) — imperceptible, but not a byte-identical no-op. Approve the consolidation, or leave both literals hardcoded and accept that /live-charts stays dark-green in light mode?

Same stray #35d07f as line 7, here as the .moveUp positive-delta text. If the consolidation is approved this becomes var(--green); note the sibling .moveDown on line 247 is #e2564a, a stray red that likewise does not match --red-ink (#e0796d) — should that be swept in the red family at the same time so up/down deltas stay a matched pair?

The livePulse keyframe here uses rgba(70, 209, 127, …) — a THIRD live green (#46d17f) distinct from both #3ed17f and #35d07f. Approve folding line 49 onto color-mix(var(--green-dot) 50%)? Dark shifts rgb(-8,0,0). Lines 50 and 51 are alpha 0 and become plain `transparent` with zero risk either way.

Section 4.6 sets --glow to `none` on paper because glows do not exist on print-like surfaces, but the eight green dot halos/pulse rings here are per-shadow literals, not the --glow token. My mapping keeps them as color-mix on --green-dot, so a live dot on paper gets a soft green halo. Should green dot glows instead be suppressed in light mode (e.g. a --green-glow token that resolves to transparent), which would also silence the pulse animations on paper?

Out-of-index sibling: .badgeDot uses `background: var(--green)` for a 6px solid dot. Under the split that should be var(--green-dot), not --green — otherwise the dot goes dark-forest on paper while the dots on every other page stay bright. Same issue at app/components/GlobeTeaser.module.css:113, app/components/mobileHome.module.css:156, app/components/todaysNumber.module.css:180, and app/globals.css:1499 (.tagLive background wash + var(--green) text). Should these bare-token sites be swept into the same patch, or handled as a separate follow-up?

The .codeAttr text sits in .codeBox, whose background is the hardcoded literal #0f0f11 (line 157) and whose sibling .codeLine is var(--gold-bright). If that code box is meant to stay a permanently dark surface (like a terminal), themed body ink (#4a443b on paper) will be invisible on it. Should the mobile code box theme to a paper surface (--bg-soft-2) so --text-body works, or stay dark — in which case this line must keep a light literal / a dedicated on-dark-code token?

The .cardEvents list sits in the floating hover card .card, whose background is the hardcoded rgba(12, 10, 9, 0.97) (line 243) — effectively --scrim, which the design says stays dark in both themes. Does this tooltip card stay dark (so its text must remain light and NOT map to --text-body), or does it become a paper card in light mode?

Approve the two new shadow primitives? The table only gives --shadow as a complete box-shadow value (geometry + colour), but 13 of my 15 drop-shadow sites have their own geometry, and this patch replaces colour LITERALS, not whole declarations — so --shadow cannot be used at 11 of them. I propose --shadow-base (light-dark(#17140f, #000000)) plus --shadow-strength (light-dark(0.31, 1)), used as color-mix(in srgb, var(--shadow-base) calc(A% * var(--shadow-strength)), transparent). Dark computes byte-identically at every site (strength 1, base #000). The 0.31 factor is not invented: it is exactly the ratio --shadow already uses (.45 dark -> .14 light), so a .45 site lands on rgba(23,20,15,.14) by construction. Alternative if you'd rather not add a strength multiplier: hand-author a light value per site.

Consolidate the twenty #000 CTA-label sites onto var(--ink-on-gold) (#14100a), accepting that dark shifts by #000 -> #14100a? Same pattern in mobileAnalysis 232/233, mobileApi 218/219, mobileCerts 418/419, mobileDeepPage 317/318, mobileMethodology 215/216, mobileMusic 189/190, mobileOfficialCharts 376/377, mobileRevenue 256/257, mobileTourMap 177/178, mobileTours 272/273. It is NOT byte-identical, so rule 1 says flag rather than round. The shift is invisible against a #ffb627 fill. Saying no is also fine — black is correct on gold in both themes, so leaving #000 is a valid no-op.

LIGHT-MODE BUG, outside my literal family but caused by it: every one of those ten CTA pills sets background-color: var(--gold) and background-image: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--gold-bright) 0%, var(--gold) 48%, var(--gold-dim) 100%). The table retires --gold to --gold-ink (#8a5a00) on paper, so on light the ramp becomes #ffd24a -> dark brown -> #c98a2e and the pill turns muddy under near-black text. These need --gold-fill, not --gold. Who owns that fix — this pass, or a separate token-alias sweep?

Three of those pills (mobileOfficialCharts ~380, mobileTourMap ~181, mobileTours ~276) re-declare color: #0a0a0b a few lines after the color: #000 in my index, so the #000 color declaration is dead and only -webkit-text-fill-color paints. Should the dead line be deleted rather than tokenised, and should the surviving #0a0a0b land on the same token I use for the -webkit line so the two paths cannot diverge?

I kept .sheet's box-shadow: 0 18px 44px rgba(0,0,0,.5) dark under rule 4 (it is the phone nav sheet, the mobile stand-in for the masthead). But the sheet deliberately stops 76px short of the bottom, so that shadow falls on live page — paper in light mode. Confirm chrome shadows keep their dark literal even where they land on the paper ground, or should this one theme while the sheet's own surface stays dark?

If the globe stage is being re-lit for paper, this shading and the gold ring/glow around it need re-authoring together — is the globe getting a light-mode treatment, or does the disc stay dark?

This family is three different near-whites doing one job: #f5f4f0 (= --text, 12 sites), #f5f0e8 (22 sites) and #ffffff (3 sites in liveCharts). Only the first is byte-identical to an existing token, so I proposed --ink-wash-base (#f5f0e8) and --white-wash-base (#ffffff) rather than round. Do you want those two tokens, or do you want to retire #f5f0e8 and #ffffff into --text the way the table already retires #cfc7bb/#d8d8de/#d3d3da into --text-body? Folding costs at most 2/255 per channel in dark mode (worst case at alpha .26; under 1/255 at the .015-.05 alphas that dominate) and deletes both proposed tokens. I did not assume it because the table blesses consolidation only for the three reading greys.

Should the whole nav get chrome-scoped token overrides (e.g. a [data-chrome] scope pinning --text/--text-muted/--line to their dark values), or should SearchPalette hardcode its own dark-chrome literals? Outside my family, but the fix has to be decided alongside it.

Confirm the Starrgirl selection fill really does stay #7a2fb0 on paper — if it is lightened for light mode, this white label must flip to dark ink at the same time or the artist's name blanks on selection.

Two car-photo badges (this one and app/records/cars/cars.module.css:290) keep light ink because they sit on background: rgba(12,10,9,0.6) — a dark scrim over a photograph. I left both literals untouched on the assumption that photo scrims stay dark on paper. Ten sites paint text on a gold fill with #0a0a0b, but the table's token for that role is --ink-on-gold = #14100a. Using the right token changes dark by 4/0/1 in RGB (invisible on a gold chip) and so breaks the strict dark-is-a-no-op rule. Do you bless --ink-on-gold as a fourth blessed consolidation for these ten, or do you want a byte-identical --ink-on-gold-cool (#0a0a0b) kept alongside it? Recommendation: bless the consolidation — two near-black inks on the same gold ramp is the drift the split is meant to end. Affects artist.module.css:493, certifications.module.css:785, StatCardMaker:76 and :141, mobileAfricasBiggest:219, mobileCerts:243, mobileOfficialCharts:380, mobileTourMap:181, mobileTours:163 and :276.

WebKit paints #000 and ignores the later declaration, so Safari and Firefox already disagree. Should all three collapse to a single color: var(--ink-on-gold) with the -webkit-text-fill-color line deleted? The #000 pair sits in the pure-black family, not the scrim family, so it needs to be patched in step with these or light mode will theme one browser and not the other.

Four chrome bars use the cool near-black (mobileAfrobeatsHub .backBar at rgba(10,10,11,.94); mobileMusic, mobileRecords, mobileLiveCharts .backBar at .95) where every other bar on the site uses --scrim's rgba(12,10,9,.94).
